answer_text:
Since  
\[
z=\rho e^{i\theta},
\]
we have
\[
z^2=\rho^2 e^{2i\theta}
=\rho^2\bigl(\cos(2\theta)+i\sin(2\theta)\bigr).
\]
Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Re}(z^2)=\rho^2\cos(2\theta).
\]

Now use the fact that for any analytic function \(g\),
\[
|e^{g(z)}|=e^{\operatorname{Re} g(z)}.
\]
Choosing \(g(z)=z^2\), define
\[
f(z)=e^{z^2}.
\]
Then \(f\) is entire, hence analytic, and
\[
|f(z)|=\left|e^{z^2}\right|
=e^{\operatorname{Re}(z^2)}
=e^{\rho^2\cos(2\theta)}.
\]

Thus one such function is

\[
\boxed{f(z)=e^{z^2}}
\]

More generally, any function of the form \(f(z)=e^{i\alpha}e^{z^2}\) with \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\) also works.
